ops.title: Sharding internal/cli across CI jobs made CI 4.5x slower, and why
ops.body:
Run `36117544647` on `perf/ci-shard` (#75) at `59f3b1e`: all 37 jobs green, total wall
clock **2795s** against a **617s** pre-sharding baseline. The regression has two
independent causes, and neither is the one the plan assumed.

## macOS runners are effectively serial here

16 macOS jobs (13 `test` shards plus the macOS legs of `rust`, `vet`, `build`).
Observed max concurrency 3. Sum of macOS job durations 2824s against 2795s of macOS
wall clock, so effective average concurrency is about **1.01**. There were 253s and
307s stretches with zero macOS jobs in flight, which the in-run 5-job cap does not
explain — it is account-wide contention for the shared five-slot pool.

The critical-path job was `test (macos-latest, 7)`. It ran for 160s and was simply
scheduled last.

Ubuntu, on the same run, hit max concurrency 10 with no throttling and finished in
**442s** — sharding works there and beats the baseline.

## The fixed per-shard cost is the -race recompile, not setup

Measured from step timestamps and raw logs: ubuntu ~27s setup plus ~86s recompile,
113s fixed; macOS ~71s plus ~52-88s, ~141s fixed. It is paid per shard regardless of
shard size. On ubuntu, 1469s of the 2140s total shard-time was fixed cost; only 671s
was test compute. The plan had budgeted a ~42s setup floor, which is what made twelve
symmetric shards look right.

## Splitting also inflated aggregate test compute about 60%

macOS aggregate test-only time across shards was ~831s against the single job's
implied ~520s — likely lost package-level parallelism inside `internal/cli`, which
`go test` exploits within one binary and cannot across `-run`-filtered sub-shards.

## Incidental finding

The repo has no required status checks at all: `gh api repos/yasyf/cc-context/rulesets`
returns `[]` and `repos/yasyf/cc-context/branches/main/protection` 404s. The
`test (ubuntu-latest)` to `test (ubuntu-latest, N)` rename could not have blocked a
merge.

## What follows

Compile the `internal/cli` test binary once per OS and share it as an artifact, which
deletes the recompile from every shard; run it from `internal/cli`, since a compiled
test binary run from the repo root fails on `testdata/` golden paths. Make the matrix
asymmetric — ubuntu keeps its shards, macOS runs minimally on pull requests and at
full strength on merge and nightly. Recompute N against the real floors rather than
the falsified 42s.
